disclaimer: Reminder reference only - NOT legal authority. Season dates, zones, and limits are set annually and can change. Always verify current regulations with the New Brunswick Department of Natural Resources and Energy Development (DNRED) before hunting or trapping. Trapping in New Brunswick is governed by the Fish and Wildlife Act and N.B. Regulation 84-124 (Fur Harvesting Regulation); seasons are in Schedule B of that regulation. The annual Hunt & Trap Regulations Summary is a plain-language guide and states that it is not a legal document. This dataset is for the separate Canada clone of Opossum Foot; it is NOT part of the US app, which stays US-only and untouched.

license_summary.carcass_submission: Every holder of a fur harvester's or minor's fur harvester's licence must deliver the entire skinned carcass (including head and organs) of every bobcat, otter, fisher and marten taken to a district ranger office not later than five days after the last day of the applicable open season; the Minister issues a receipt for each carcass (s. 4.2(1)-(2)).
license_summary.certified_traps: Only AIHTS-certified traps may be used where Reg. 84-124 prescribes them: killing traps for beaver, raccoon, muskrat, weasel, marten, fisher and otter must be Schedule A traps (s. 4(4.01)(a)); bobcat killing traps must be Schedule A traps and only from the Saturday of the second week in November to December 31 (s. 4(4.01)(c)); early-season raccoon trapping requires Schedule A.1 restraining traps (s. 4(4)(f.4)); bobcat leg-hold traps must be Schedule A.2 traps; beaver live holding traps must be Schedule A.3 traps (s. 4(4.02)). Killing traps are prohibited for coyote and fox (s. 4(4.01)(b)). See the aihts object.
license_summary.course: Before a first fur harvester's licence is issued, the applicant must show proof of (a) a recognized firearm safety and hunter education course (or bow hunter education, if hunting by bow/crossbow) and (b) a recognized trapper education course (s. 4(1.2)). Both course requirements are waived for an applicant born before January 1, 1981 who proves previous holding of the corresponding licence (ss. 4(1.201), 4(1.202)). Minors 12-15 must meet the same course requirements (s. 4(1.11)); a minor 10-11 may hunt, trap or snare only when accompanied at all times by an adult fur harvester licence holder (s. 4(1.12)), and minors under 12 may not carry a firearm (s. 4(4.5)).
license_summary.export_permits: An export permit under Fish and Wildlife Act s. 91 for bobcat, otter, fisher or marten pelts is issued only against the carcass receipts tendered - one pelt per receipt (s. 4.2(3)-(4)). Bobcat and river otter are CITES-listed; exporting their pelts from Canada also requires a CITES export permit (Hunt & Trap guide). Parts of fur bearing animals that may be bought, sold, bartered or exported are the claws, teeth, urine, tail, prepared pelt and scent glands of lawfully taken animals (s. 4.3).
license_summary.fees: Fees are set in Reg. 84-124 s. 18: fur harvester's licence $43 (under 65) / $22 (65 and over); minor's fur harvester's licence $0; application for a bobcat authorization $9; rabbit licence $8; minor's rabbit licence $0; resident fur trader's licence $37.50; non-resident fur trader's licence $150; resident hide dealer's licence $22.50; non-resident hide dealer's licence $75; replacement licence $5.25. A $5 conservation fee (Wildlife Trust Fund) is added to a fur harvester's licence or rabbit licence at purchase (s. 18.1) - so a rabbit licence costs $13.00 in total, matching the guide. The guide shows the bobcat application as '$9 plus HST'; whether HST applies to the licence fees themselves was not verified in this pass (see known gaps).
license_summary.fur_harvesters_licence: A fur harvester's licence (Fish and Wildlife Act s. 83; Reg. 84-124 s. 4(1)(a)) is required to hunt, trap or snare fur bearing animals and to possess or sell pelts. Issued to New Brunswick residents only, 16 years of age or over; NOT issued to non-residents (Hunt & Trap guide). A minor's fur harvester's licence covers ages 10-15 (s. 4(1)(c)). The licence expires annually on July 31 (s. 4(2)(a)); the guide states it is valid from October 1 to July 31 of the following year.
license_summary.harvest_report: Reg. 84-124 contains no Ontario-style mandatory season-end harvest report for fur harvesters. Reporting obligations are: the carcass-submission rule for bobcat, otter, fisher and marten (s. 4.2); a licence holder's duty to furnish information and wildlife parts when required by the Minister (s. 4(3)); the raccoon night-hunting permit report due January 31 (s. 13(3)(a)); the special coyote control permit report due within 14 days after the permit expires (s. 4.1(5)); and fur trader / hide dealer record-keeping and periodic reports (ss. 5, 8). DNRED publishes an annual Furbearer Harvest Report compiled from these sources.
license_summary.hunting_furbearers: The fur harvester's licence also covers hunting bobcat, fox, skunk, raccoon, coyote, squirrel and rabbit (varying hare) in season (s. 4(1)(a)(i)). Raccoon and skunk may also be hunted under a Bird and Small Game Licence or Deer and Game Bird Licence (Oct. 1 - Dec. 31, no limit). Coyote may also be hunted under a Varmint Licence (March-September) and under a Bear Licence during bear seasons. Hunting with hounds requires Minister-approved hounds and a permit (ss. 13, 15; maximum three hounds for bobcat or fox). Sunday hunting is restricted in New Brunswick under the Hunting Regulation; the general rule was not transcribed into this dataset (see known gaps).
license_summary.licence_types: Fur harvester's licence; minor's fur harvester's licence; rabbit licence; minor's rabbit licence; fur trader's licence (resident / non-resident); hide dealer's licence (resident / non-resident). Overlays: bobcat authorization with lock seal bobcat tags (draw); hound hunting permits (ss. 13, 15); special coyote control permit (s. 4.1); possession/cold-storage permits (s. 7).
license_summary.outdoors_card: An Outdoors Card number is required to purchase an angling, hunting or trapping licence, to apply to draws, and to register for a Conservation Education course. Registration is one-time and free; the card is not a licence and need not be carried (DNRED Outdoors Card page).
license_summary.permission: Unlike Ontario, Reg. 84-124 does not tie the licence to designated land and contains no registered-trapline system: the fur harvester's licence is valid by WMZ anywhere in the province (subject to the zone closures in s. 4(1.1)). No registered trapline / Crown land trapline tenure was found in the Fish and Wildlife Act or Reg. 84-124 in this pass - a negative finding flagged for DNRED confirmation (see known gaps). Traps or snares may not be disturbed by anyone but the owner or a conservation officer (s. 17). Wildlife Refuges and listed Wildlife Management Areas, parks and historical sites are closed to hunting, trapping and snaring (Hunt & Trap guide). Landowner-permission and trespass rules outside Reg. 84-124 were not verified in this pass.
license_summary.quotas: There are no bag limits in New Brunswick fur harvesting except rabbit (varying hare): daily 10, possession 20 (s. 4(8)). The one quota-controlled species is bobcat: the Minister sets an annual quota range for each of WMZs 1-25 (and may set zero), and authorizations are allocated by random computer draw so the number of lock seal tags issued falls within the range (s. 4.01(5)-(6)).
license_summary.report_violation: Report violations and illegal hunting, fishing and wood theft to Crime Stoppers at 1-800-222-TIPS (8477) or to a local DNRED office (DNRED 'Report Violations' page; the program is known as Target Poaching).
license_summary.tagging: Bobcat pelts must be tagged immediately on killing (hunting) or on taking possession (trapping/snaring) with a previously unused lock seal bobcat tag issued to that person, inserted through the eye hole and mouth of the pelt with the locking mechanism fully engaged (s. 4.02). Possession of an untagged bobcat pelt is prohibited. No other furbearer requires a pelt tag in Reg. 84-124.
license_summary.trap_check: Every restraining trap, live holding trap, leg hold trap, box trap or leg snare - excluding drowning sets - must be checked at least once every 48 hours after setting, and any wildlife taken must be removed immediately (s. 4(4.1)). All traps and snares must be removed not later than sunset on the last day of the open season (s. 4(5)). No person may possess a trap or snare in a resort of wildlife in a WMZ more than 48 hours before the season opens or more than 48 hours after it ends (s. 4(4.2)).
license_summary.where_to_buy: Licences are available through the Fish and Wildlife Licensing System at gnb.ca/fishwildlife, from authorized vendors, and at all Service New Brunswick centres (Hunt & Trap guide).
license_summary.zones: Seasons are keyed to Wildlife Management Zones (WMZs) 1-27, established under s. 12 of the Hunting Regulation (N.B. Reg. 84-133) and adopted for fur harvesting by Reg. 84-124 s. 3. Zone groupings used by Schedule B: 1-27 (province-wide), 1-12 / 13-27 (water furbearers), 1-26 (coyote/fox), 1-12 / 13-26 (coyote/fox snaring), 1-25 (bobcat), 1-12 / 13-25 (bobcat snaring), and 1-13, 15-17, 20 / 14, 18, 19, 21-27 (fisher/marten/skunk). WMZ 27 is Grand Manan Island.

bag_limits.limit_notes: No bag limit in Schedule B; harvest is controlled by quota and tags. A bobcat authorization is issued by random computer draw (one application per year, $9 application fee, applications close the last Friday of September - September 25, 2026). The Minister sets an annual quota range for each of WMZs 1-25 and may set a quota of zero. species.notes: Tagging is mandatory and immediate: on killing or taking possession of a bobcat, the hunter/trapper must affix an unused lock seal bobcat tag through the eye hole and the mouth of the pelt and fully engage the lock (s. 4.02). verification.confirmation_notes: All season dates are from Schedule B of N.B. Reg. 84-124 (Fur Harvesting Regulation), consolidated to April 21, 2026 including amendments to 2026-21, read in full 2026-11-15. Schedule B states seasons as relative dates; each was computed for 2026-27 and verified by calendar check: last Saturday in October 2026 = October 31; second last Saturday in October = October 24; first Saturday after October 28 = October 31; first Monday in August 2026 = August 3; with the regulation's Sunday-start definition of 'week' (s. 2), the Saturday of the first week of November 2026 = November 7 and of the second week = November 14; last Saturday in November = November 28, the second Saturday thereafter = December 12 and the third Saturday thereafter = December 19; last day of February 2027 = February 28 (2027 is not a leap year); last day of January = January 31, 2027; last day of December = December 31, 2026; fourth Sunday of January 2027 = January 24; Friday before the last Saturday in October = October 30, 2026; last Friday of September 2026 = September 25 (bobcat draw application deadline - matches the guide); Saturday of the third week of March 2027 = March 27 (weeks counted Sunday-start; the first week of March 2027 begins Sunday March 7, so the third week is March 21-27). Every computed date was cross-checked against the 2026-27 Hunt & Trap guide's Fur Harvesting Seasons table (p. 43): all trapping and snaring dates agree exactly, including the guide's printed spring muskrat opener of March 27, 2027, the fisher/marten/skunk windows of November 28 - December 12 and November 28 - December 19, and the beaver snaring close of February 28. The only disagreements are the hunting close dates in known_gaps. Licence fees cross-check: the guide's rabbit licence price of $13.00 equals the regulation's $8 fee plus the $5 conservation fee (ss. 18, 18.1). Zone closures in s. 4(1.1) (bobcat in WMZs 26-27; marten in WMZs 14, 18, 19, 21-27; coyote/fox in WMZ 27) agree with the zone groups printed in Schedule B and the guide. Beaver snaring: Schedule B prints the snaring close (last day in February) against the trapping row; the guide confirms snaring opens on the trapping opener in both zone groups.
known_gaps: Hunting close dates: the 2026-27 guide's Fur Harvesting Seasons table prints February 27, 2027 as the close of the hunting seasons for rabbit, squirrel, coyote/fox and bobcat, where Schedule B of the regulation says 'last day in February' (February 28, 2027) for the combined rows. The dataset follows the regulation (the law; the guide states it is not a legal document), and the affected hunting rows carry a note. DNRED confirmation is needed before the dataset is treated as final - this is the single open date question in the pass.

The official Hunt & Trap 2026-27 PDF (www2.gnb.ca) and several gnb.ca content pages returned HTTP 403 to this session's fetcher and could not be read directly. The guide's season table was cross-checked via its published tables as transcribed with page citations, and DNRED's own publications (Furbearer Harvest Report, Species at Risk Registry, Outdoors Card and Report Violations pages) were read via the search index. Re-verify the dataset against the official PDF itself before build.

Registered traplines: no registered-trapline or Crown-land trapline tenure system was found in the Fish and Wildlife Act, in Reg. 84-124 (read in full), or in DNRED material surfaced in this pass. This is a negative finding, not a verified absence - one confirmation question to DNRED settles it. If a trapline system does exist outside the fur harvesting regulation, the clone may need a trapline field the dataset does not have.

HST on fees: the guide shows the bobcat authorization application as '$9 plus HST'. Whether HST is added to the fur harvester's, rabbit and other licence fees in s. 18 was not verified; the dataset records the regulation's fees and the $5 conservation fee only.

Sunday hunting: New Brunswick restricts hunting on Sundays under the Hunting Regulation (N.B. Reg. 84-133). The 2026-27 guide's general rule (hunting permitted only on Sundays falling between October 14 and December 31, as transcribed from the guide's general regulations) was not verified against Reg. 84-133 in this pass, and no Sunday rule is encoded in the season rows (open_time is null throughout). Verify before the clone displays hunting days.

Hound hunting and training seasons for fox and bobcat (guide pp. 38-39: training October 14 - February 27; hound hunting November 14 - February 27, permits under ss. 13 and 15) are permit overlays and are recorded in species notes, not as separate season rows. Only raccoon's hunting-with-hounds season, which appears in Schedule B itself, is modelled as a row.

Cougar and gray wolf protection-status wording: both are closed because Schedule B gives them no season and the fur harvester's licence does not cover them. No NB Species at Risk Registry listing for cougar was found, and the registry entry for gray wolf was not individually pulled in this pass (wolverine and lynx registry entries were). Confirm the status wording with DNRED before publishing closed-species notes.

French versions were not reviewed. New Brunswick is officially bilingual and every instrument used here (Reg. 84-124, the Hunt & Trap guide, DNRED pages) is published in French as well ('Reglement sur la recolte de fourrures', 'Chasse et piegeage'). No French-only material was encountered, but a bilingual dataset/UI pass is a real follow-on cost for this province - larger than for Ontario.

WMZ boundary data is not in this pass (same as Ontario): the dataset references WMZ groups only. A WMZ picker list is the minimum viable approach for the clone; boundary/map lookup is a separate task.

Nuisance wildlife control (N.B. Reg. 97-141, nuisance wildlife operator licences - including the 72-hour beaver trap/snare check for operators added by Reg. 2026-22) is a separate permit regime and is out of scope for this dataset.

Black bear is not a fur bearing animal under Reg. 84-124 and has no trapping season in New Brunswick; it is hunted under a separate Bear Licence (Hunting Regulation) and is therefore excluded from this dataset, unlike Ontario where bear trapping exists.

aihts.note: New Brunswick implements the AIHTS through N.B. Reg. 84-124 s. 4(4.01)-(4.02) and its own schedules: Schedule A (certified killing traps), Schedule A.1 (certified restraining traps - raccoon), Schedule A.2 (certified leg-hold traps - bobcat), Schedule A.3 (certified live holding traps - beaver). DNRED's Furbearer Harvest Report states that since the 2007 season the regulations have been changed so that only certified traps are allowed for beaver, fisher, marten, raccoon and muskrat, and points trappers to the certified trap list printed in the Hunt & Trap Summary; the regulation's schedules in fact extend certified-trap requirements to otter, weasel and (conditionally) bobcat as well. The schedules track the Fur Institute of Canada national certified-trap list (updated July 22, 2026). AIHTS was agreed in 1997 and ratified by Canada in June 1999; it covers 12 North American species.
trap_rules: Only Schedule A killing traps may be used for beaver, raccoon, muskrat, weasel, marten, fisher or otter (Reg. 84-124 s. 4(4.01)(a)).
Killing traps are prohibited for coyote and fox (s. 4(4.01)(b)).
Killing traps for bobcat: Schedule A traps only, and only from the Saturday of the second week in November to December 31; prohibited January 1 to the last day of February (s. 4(4.01)(c)).

Only Schedule A.3 live holding traps may be used for beaver (s. 4(4.02)); only Schedule A.2 leg-hold traps may be used for bobcat (s. 4(4)(f.1)(i.02)); raccoon trapping October 1-30 requires Schedule A.1 restraining traps (s. 4(4)(f.4)).

Leg-hold traps: fox - jaw spread 20 cm or less, no running pole or spring pole set; coyote - jaw spread 20 cm or less, jaws laminated, offset or padded, no running pole or spring pole set; beaver, muskrat, otter and mink - drowning sets only, jaw spread 22 cm or less (s. 4(4)(f.1)).

Toothed traps, deadfalls and hooks are prohibited (s. 4(4)(f)). No trap or snare inside a muskrat house (s. 4(4)(b)). Weasel and squirrel traps must be entirely enclosed in a wooden or metal box with no opening larger than 3.75 cm (s. 4(4)(e.1)).

Mink traps: on the ground within three metres of the water's edge, or a water-base set or drowning set (s. 4(4)(f.2)). Beaver snares from the fourth Sunday of January to the season close must be baited with fresh hardwood and placed entirely underwater (s. 4(4)(f.3)).

Snares (other than power snares) of wire over 0.75 mm diameter must have a locking device (s. 4(4)(d.1)). No setting traps or snares between the close of the fox season and the opening of the muskrat season except for rabbit (s. 4(4)(e)).
Trap check: restraining, live holding, leg hold and box traps and leg snares (excluding drowning sets) at least once every 48 hours (s. 4(4.1)).

aihts.canada_wide: AIHTS in force in Canada since 1 June 1999 (Canada, the EU and Russia are parties; the US is not a party). FIC-certified traps mandatory per Phase 1 lists - killing traps: beaver, Canada lynx & bobcat, fisher, marten, muskrat (on land and underwater), otter, raccoon, weasels/ermine; restraining traps: beaver (cage), bobcat, Canada lynx, raccoon, wolf. Conventional steel-jawed leghold restraining traps on land are effectively banned for AIHTS species. Killing neck snares are NOT AIHTS traps and are not FIC-certified; provinces regulate snares separately. [R1 s.2a]
aihts.jurisdiction_specific: New Brunswick is a FIC Note 1 province (exclusive use of certified restraining traps for raccoon). Secondary reporting puts certified coyote restraining traps mandatory in 2029-30. [R1 s.2a]

check_interval.live_holding: Restraining, live-holding, leg-hold, box traps and leg snares (excluding drowning sets): 48 hours (Reg. 2023-12 amending Fur Harvesting Reg. s. 4(4.1)).
check_interval.killing: Beaver killing traps/drowning sets under an operator's licence: 72 hours (Reg. 2026-22); no interval stated for other killing traps. Nuisance Wildlife Control Operator work: traps/snares every 24 hours, beaver sets every 72 hours.

canada_only.tenure: No registered trapline system found - Fur Harvester's Licence is zone-based (Wildlife Management Zones 1-27).
canada_only.trap_id_requirement: PARTIAL - only holders of a special coyote control permit must affix the permit number to all traps and snares used under it (Fur Harvesting Regulation 84-124 s. 4.1(4)). No general trap-marking requirement for ordinary fur harvesters found. [R2 Item 6]
canada_only.royalty: None found in the Fish and Wildlife Act, Fur Harvesting Regulation 84-124, or GNB licence pages. [R2 Item 5]
canada_only.nuisance_route: Paid route exists - a Nuisance Wildlife Control Operator's Licence is required to operate (or work for) a nuisance wildlife control enterprise, i.e. removing/relocating nuisance wildlife for consideration (NB Reg 97-141; issued by the Minister; expires Dec 31; records per animal and an annual report due Jan 14). Kill or relocate both allowed, except six rabies-vector species (raccoon, skunk, fox, coyote, groundhog, mink) may not be relocated and must be humanely euthanized; bat work needs a separate permit. Verified in regulation text. [R2 Item 3]
canada_only.harvest_reporting_and_sealing: Bobcat, marten and otter carcasses must go to a district office within 5 days after season close, with trapper name, licence number and WMZ of capture - an offence to fail. Bobcat pelts need lock-seal tags attached through lip to eyehole immediately on taking possession; only properly tagged pelts may be possessed/sold. [R1 s.5]
